phases.name: Power and Repeatability
phases.goal: Raise ability to repeatedly hit threshold and recover quickly

phases.name: Ace Peloton Simulation
phases.goal: Simulate race fatigue, surge-recover patterns, peloton dynamics

phases.name: Taper and Sharpen
phases.goal: Reduce fatigue while preserving sharpness and neuromuscular readiness

sessions.title: Day 1 Benchmark
sessions.description: Data-gathering sessions. Kona benchmark AM. High Cadence Drills PM. Establish baseline cadence, HR, power profile.
sessions.notes: Discovered natural cadence 61 RPM. Proven ceiling 111 RPM. KICKR confirmed. Gearing issue identified and resolved mid-session.

sessions.title: Full Recovery
sessions.description: Complete rest. Mobility work only. Two-a-day on Day 1 requires full recovery window. Adaptation happens now.
sessions.notes: Fix front derailleur. Order Intake breathing magnets. Research trainer bike.

sessions.title: Threshold Builder
sessions.description: 4x8 min at 95-100% FTP. 4 min recovery between. ERG OFF. Teaching your body to stay uncomfortable without exploding. Most important energy system for fondo survival.
sessions.notes: ERG OFF — Tulsa requires self-managed pacing. Watch cadence — target 88+ throughout.

sessions.title: Endurance + Sweet Spot
sessions.description: 2-3 hrs. 3x12 min at 88-92% FTP. The diesel engine zone. Biggest ROI training zone for fondo performance. Use pace partners at 2.0-2.3 W/kg.
sessions.notes: First long session. Practice fueling — 60g carbs/hr minimum. Use pace partners to simulate peloton drafting.

sessions.title: Full Recovery
sessions.description: No rides. No ego. If legs feel amazing — good. Do not ruin the adaptation window. Sleep, fuel, hydrate.
sessions.notes: Mobility work approved. Box breathing practice.

sessions.title: Ace Peloton Simulation
sessions.description: 40s at 120% FTP / 20s recovery. 2 sets of 10 reps. 8 min rest between sets. Simulates peloton surges, corner exits, small climbs. KEY: recovery while still moving fast.
sessions.notes: Should feel progressively accumulating stress — NOT total failure. If you detonate you went too hard.

sessions.title: Aerobic Consolidation
sessions.description: 90-120 min strict Z2. Adaptation happens during recovery from intensity. Use pace partners at 2.0 W/kg. Practice sitting in draft — do NOT pull through.
sessions.notes: Peloton sim focus — practice drafting efficiency with pace partners. Conservation over power.

sessions.title: Threshold Extension
sessions.description: 5x8 min at 95% FTP. Building on Day 3. Recovery 3 min. Notice if effort feels easier — that is adaptation working.
sessions.notes: Compare cadence and HR to Day 3. Improvement here confirms adaptation.

sessions.title: Active Recovery
sessions.description: 45 min easy spin. Check HR vs Day 2 warmup — should be lower at same watts. That delta is fitness.
sessions.notes: High cadence recovery drill. Compare natural cadence to Day 1 baseline of 61 RPM.

sessions.title: Mid-Block Long Ride
sessions.description: 3-4 hrs. Half-block checkpoint ride. Sweet spot blocks in second half. Note fatigue profile vs Day 4. Fueling discipline critical.
sessions.notes: Kona again — compare to Day 1 benchmark. Same route, different rider. Note cadence and HR drift differences.

sessions.title: Mid-Block Rest
sessions.description: Full rest. Mid-block recovery window. Sleep, fuel, hydrate. This is training. Do not skip this.
sessions.notes: Assess mid-block stability score trend. If 3-day average below 55 — flag for adaptation.

sessions.title: Race Attacks
sessions.description: 30s at 130% FTP / 30s float. 3 sets of 8 reps. Simulates peloton attacks, corner exits, small punchy climbs. Fixed gear attack instincts apply here.
sessions.notes: Your fixed gear crit background is an asset here. Urban attack instincts translate. Use them.

sessions.title: Sustained Threshold
sessions.description: 2x20 min at 88-92% FTP. Longest sustained effort of the block. Mental durability training. This is where Tulsa survival gets built.
sessions.notes: Longest threshold effort of block. Note when it gets hard mentally — that timing is data.

sessions.title: Endurance Flush
sessions.description: 2 hrs Z2. Recovery-adjacent. Focus entirely on fueling practice — 60-80g carbs/hr minimum. Pace partner drafting practice.
sessions.notes: Fueling dress rehearsal. Practice exactly what you will do race day. No experimenting on race day.

sessions.title: Rest Day
sessions.description: Full rest. Three hard blocks completed. Trust what you have built. The work is done.
sessions.notes: Taper phase begins. Volume drops 40% from here.

sessions.title: Final Sharpener
sessions.description: Short VO2 microburst session. Maintain neuromuscular sharpness without accumulating fatigue. 20 min max hard effort total.
sessions.notes: Short and sharp. In and out. Do not linger.

sessions.title: Pre-Taper Ride
sessions.description: 2 hrs. Include 3x5 min at threshold to stay sharp. This is the last load day of the block.
sessions.notes: Last load day. Note how 88+ RPM feels compared to Day 1 natural cadence of 61.

sessions.title: Taper Begins
sessions.description: Volume drops 40%. 60 min easy. Legs may feel heavy — that is glycogen loading and muscle repair. It is correct.
sessions.notes: Heavy legs during taper is normal. Do not panic. Do not add extra sessions.

sessions.title: Taper Day 2
sessions.description: 45 min. Include 3x1 min at race pace to keep neuromuscular system primed. Then shut it down completely.
sessions.notes: Three sharp 1-min efforts to remind your legs what fast feels like. Then done.

sessions.title: Pre-Race Rest
sessions.description: Full rest or 20 min shake-out spin maximum. Eat. Sleep. Trust everything you have built over 20 days.
sessions.notes: Race is June 6. This is May 26. You have 11 days between block end and race. Use them well.
